articles.title: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days 2026: Best stargazing deals on telescopes and binoculars
articles.author: Kimberley Lane

paras.en: Amazon Big Deal Days is back, and we've found some tempting deals on our favorite stargazing equipment at Amazon. For the next two days (Tuesday, Oct. 6 and Wednesday, October 7, 2026), we'll be keeping our eyes on the sales so you can keep your eyes on the skies.
paras.zh: 亚马逊大优惠日又回来了，我们在亚马逊上发现了一些我们最喜欢的观星设备的诱人优惠。在接下来的两天（2026 年 10 月 6 日星期二和 10 月 7 日星期三），我们将密切关注销售情况，以便您可以密切关注天空。

paras.en: Fall is a fantastic time to stargaze, with meteor showers, full moons, constellations and planetary oppositions — some of which you can only see with binoculars or a telescope. Shop the best deals on telescopes and binoculars below.
paras.zh: 秋天是观星的绝佳时机，有流星雨、满月、星座和行星对立——其中一些只能用双筒望远镜或天文望远镜才能看到。在下面购买望远镜和双筒望远镜的超值优惠。

paras.en: If you want a small, easy-to-use smart telescope with minimal investment, you can save $99 on the ZWO Seestar S30.
paras.zh: 如果您想要一台小型、易于使用的智能望远镜，并且投资最少，那么购买 ZWO Seestar S30 可以节省 99 美元。

paras.en: These small smart telescopes are ideal for deep-sky astrophotography, particularly for large nebulas and galaxies like the North America Nebula and the Andromeda Galaxy. They're an easy introduction to astrophotography, and you can also photograph the Moon and Sun, too.
paras.zh: 这些小型智能望远镜非常适合深空天文摄影，特别是北美星云和仙女座星系等大型星云和星系。它们是天文摄影的简单入门，您还可以拍摄月亮和太阳。

paras.en: Although we haven't reviewed this exact model, you can read our review of the S30 Pro, which we named the best portable smart telescope.
paras.zh: 虽然我们还没有评测过这个确切的型号，但您可以阅读我们对 S30 Pro 的评测，我们将其称为最佳便携式智能望远镜。

paras.en: If you want a portable smart telescope that excels at wide-angle shooting, the Dwarf Mini is the ideal choice, and you can save $59 right now at Amazon.
paras.zh: 如果您想要一款擅长广角拍摄的便携式智能望远镜，Dwarf Mini 是理想的选择，现在您可以在亚马逊节省 59 美元。

paras.en: Its portability is the killer feature here, as it's around half the weight of the Seestar S30 we mentioned above. Plus, the wide-angle camera is much wider, making it better for Milky Way landscapes, constellations and bigger portions of the sky.
paras.zh: 它的便携性是这里的杀手锏，因为它的重量约为我们上面提到的 Seestar S30 的一半。此外，广角相机更宽，更适合拍摄银河系景观、星座和更大的天空部分。

paras.en: Read our full Dwarflab Dwarf Mini review
paras.zh: 阅读我们完整的 Dwarflab Dwarf Mini 评论

paras.en: This small, portable Celestron telescope is ideal for beginners and younger users who want a closer look at the Moon and planets.
paras.zh: 这款小型便携式星特朗望远镜非常适合想要近距离观察月球和行星的初学者和年轻用户。

paras.en: Not to be confused with the Celestron AstroMaster LT 70AZ, which is smaller and gives you a slightly wider view. The standard AstroMaster 70AZ, which is on offer here, has a longer focal length, which is better suited to spotting planets, particularly Jupiter and Saturn. This telescope usually sits around $179, and this is the cheapest we've seen it since June.
paras.zh: 不要与星特朗 AstroMaster LT 70AZ 混淆，后者更小，视野稍宽。这里提供的标准 AstroMaster 70AZ 具有更长的焦距，更适合发现行星，特别是木星和土星。这台望远镜的价格通常约为 179 美元，这是自 6 月份以来我们见过的最便宜的价格。

paras.en: The Celestron StarSense range is really useful for total beginners, as the smartphone dock and accompanying app work out where the telescope is pointing, then show arrows on the screen to guide you towards certain objects.
paras.zh: 星特朗 StarSense 系列对于初学者来说非常有用，因为智能手机底座和随附的应用程序会计算出望远镜指向的位置，然后在屏幕上显示箭头以引导您走向某些物体。

paras.en: So, rather than "Here's a telescope, good luck finding Jupiter", the StarSense is much more "Here's what's visible tonight. Pick something, and I'll show you where it is".
paras.zh: 因此，StarSense 与其说是“这是一架望远镜，祝你好运找到木星”，不如说是“这是今晚可见的东西。选择一些东西，我会告诉你它在哪里”。

paras.en: If you can afford to stretch your budget, this is a better option than the AstroMaster 70LT we listed above. It has better light-gathering capabilities thanks to the wider aperture; it's a lighter package overall and it includes a 2x Barlow lens.
paras.zh: 如果您有足够的预算，这是比我们上面列出的 AstroMaster 70LT 更好的选择。由于光圈更大，因此具有更好的聚光能力；总体而言，它是一个更轻的包装，并且包含一个 2x Barlow 镜头。

paras.en: We've not reviewed the 80mm aperture model, but we do have a full Celestron StarSense Explorer LT 70AZ review.
paras.zh: 我们还没有评测过 80mm 光圈型号，但我们确实有完整的星特朗 StarSense Explorer LT 70AZ 评测。

paras.en: If you're looking for more of an intermediate-level telescope, the Celestron AstroMaster 130EQ-MD is a great option, and you can save $58 right now.
paras.zh: 如果您正在寻找更多的中级望远镜，星特朗 AstroMaster 130EQ-MD 是一个不错的选择，您现在可以节省 58 美元。

paras.en: The EQ mount has a bit of a learning curve, but once you've got it set up, it's a much more accurate way of tracking objects across the night sky. Plus, this version comes with a motor drive, so there's no manual adjusting needed.
paras.zh: EQ 安装座有一定的学习曲线，但一旦设置完毕，它就是一种更准确地跟踪夜空中物体的方法。另外，该版本配有电机驱动，因此无需手动调节。

paras.en: The 130mm aperture is great for viewing brighter deep-sky objects, and the moon looks beautiful, as do Jupiter and Saturn.
paras.zh: 130 毫米光圈非常适合观看更明亮的深空天体，月亮、木星和土星看起来都很美丽。

paras.en: If you like the intelligence of a smart telescope but want an observational telescope, a GoTo is the perfect combination. Once the telescope is aligned, you use the handset to select a celestial object from the list, and the telescope automatically orients itself toward your chosen object.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢智能望远镜的智能性，但想要一台观测望远镜，GoTo 是完美的组合。望远镜对准后，您可以使用手机从列表中选择一个天体，望远镜会自动将其朝向您选择的天体。

paras.en: This telescope has a 102mm aperture, which is excellent for observing larger deep-sky objects, the moon, and planets. It's user-friendly without feeling too much like a beginner telescope, and it's an excellent price.
paras.zh: 该望远镜的口径为 102 毫米，非常适合观测较大的深空天体、月球和行星。它用户友好，不会感觉太像初学者望远镜，而且价格也很优惠。

paras.en: These massive, powerful astronomy binoculars are the closest thing to a telescope that isn't actually a telescope. With 25x magnification and 100mm objective lens diameter, they're perfect for getting detailed views of the moon and night sky.
paras.zh: 这些巨大而强大的天文双筒望远镜是最接近望远镜的东西，但实际上并不是望远镜。它们具有 25 倍放大倍率和 100 毫米物镜直径，非常适合获取月亮和夜空的详细视图。

paras.en: Be warned, they're very big and very heavy, so you'll need to mount them on a tripod. They're for dedicated astronomy users, so if you want something lightweight and portable, check out some of the other options in this guide.
paras.zh: 请注意，它们非常大且非常重，因此您需要将它们安装在三脚架上。它们适用于专门的天文学用户，因此如果您想要轻巧便携的东西，请查看本指南中的一些其他选项。

paras.en: Read our full Celestron SkyMaster 25x100 review
paras.zh: 阅读我们完整的星特朗 SkyMaster 25x100 评论

paras.en: If you're looking for astronomy binoculars on a budget, these 12x60s from Celestron are ideal. They're a little big to use handheld, but they'll give you great views of the moon and stars, and you'll be able to spot Jupiter's moons.
paras.zh: 如果您正在寻找预算有限的天文双筒望远镜，星特朗的这些 12x60 双筒望远镜是您的理想选择。它们对于手持使用来说有点大，但它们可以让你看到月亮和星星的美景，而且你还可以发现木星的卫星。

paras.en: Read our full Celestron SkyMaster 12x60 review
paras.zh: 阅读我们完整的星特朗 SkyMaster 12x60 评论

paras.en: Binoculars with viewing power and excellent optical quality. These binoculars have ED glass to eliminate chromatic aberration, which is particularly useful when viewing the moon. They're more of an investment than non-ED glass, but they're worth every cent and will last a long time.
paras.zh: 具有可视能力和出色光学质量的双筒望远镜。这些双筒望远镜采用 ED 玻璃来消除色差，这在观看月球时特别有用。与非 ED 玻璃相比，它们更像是一种投资，但它们物有所值，并且可以使用很长时间。

paras.en: We've not reviewed this exact variant, but we have a full review of the smaller Celestron Nature DX ED 10x42.
paras.zh: 我们还没有审查过这个确切的变体，但我们对较小的星特朗 Nature DX ED 10x42 进行了全面审查。

paras.en: The Celestron Regal ED 10x42 is one of the best multi-use binoculars we've tested. The ED glass and field-flattening technology produce clear, sharp views across the entire frame, and the 10x42 spec is good for spotting wildlife and sweeping across the sky to get a closer look at the moon and stars.
paras.zh: Celestron Regal ED 10x42 是我们测试过的最好的多用途双筒望远镜之一。 ED 玻璃和视场平坦技术可在整个画面上产生清晰锐利的视野，10x42 规格非常适合发现野生动物和扫过天空以近距离观察月亮和星星。

paras.en: Read our full Celestron Regal ED 10x42 review
paras.zh: 阅读我们完整的星特朗 Regal ED 10x42 评论

paras.zh: 将世界上最迷人的发现直接发送到您的收件箱。

With over 6 years of photography experience, her skills span across landscape and seascape photography, wildlife, astrophotography and portrait work. Her photos have been featured in a number of national magazines, including Digital Camera World and Cosmopolitan. She has also contributed to our sister site Space.com and Tech Radar, and she regularly uses binoculars and telescopes to stargaze in the dark skies of South Wales.
paras.zh: Live Science 的电子商务撰稿人 Kimberley Lane 测试了多种光学设备，评测了索尼、佳能、OM System 等公司的相机设备。她拥有超过 6 年的摄影经验，技能涵盖风景和海景摄影、野生动物、天文摄影和肖像作品。她的照片曾出现在许多国家杂志上，包括《数码相机世界》和《Cosmopolitan》。她还为我们的姊妹网站 Space.com 和 Tech Radar 做出了贡献，她经常使用双筒望远镜和天文望远镜在南威尔士的黑暗天空中观察星空。

articles.title: Could 2026 Be a Year With No Atlantic Hurricanes? We've Surprisingly Passed Their Peak Month Without Any, Thanks to the El Niño

paras.en: Hurricanes usually wreak havoc in the Atlantic Ocean from June through November. But four months into this year’s season, we haven’t seen a storm escalate into a hurricane—and may not at all. That’s likely thanks to the “super” El Niño, which seems to be suppressing cyclones in the Atlantic while fueling them in the Pacific Ocean.
paras.zh: 飓风通常在六月到十一月期间对大西洋造成严重破坏。但今年季节已经过去四个月了，我们还没有看到风暴升级为飓风——而且可能根本没有。这可能要归功于“超级”厄尔尼诺现象，它似乎抑制了大西洋的气旋，同时又助长了太平洋的气旋。

paras.en: “No hurricanes through September is unprecedented in the modern record, and it’s a little surreal to look at the maps every day this month and see the deep tropics basically shut off,” says Michael Lowry, a meteorologist and hurricane specialist with WPLG-TV, to Andrea Thompson at Scientific American.
paras.zh: WPLG-TV 的气象学家兼飓风专家迈克尔·劳里 (Michael Lowry) 对《科学美国人》的安德里亚·汤普森 (Andrea Thompson) 表示：“整个 9 月都没有出现飓风，这在现代记录中是史无前例的，这个月每天查看地图，看到深热带地区基本被封锁，这有点超现实。”

paras.en: A hurricane-free September is surprising because the 10th of the month is statistically the peak of Atlantic hurricane season. This marks the first time in more than 30 years that the month has passed without one of these powerful storms. According to modern records stretching back to 1950, they have occurred only in 1994, 1972 and 1962, Phil Klotzbach, a hurricane expert at Colorado State University, tells Chris Dolce at CNN.
paras.zh: 9 月没有飓风令人惊讶，因为据统计，该月 10 日是大西洋飓风季节的高峰期。这是 30 多年来第一次没有发生如此强大风暴的月份。科罗拉多州立大学的飓风专家 Phil Klotzbach 告诉 CNN 的 Chris Dolce，根据可追溯到 1950 年的现代记录，这些飓风仅在 1994 年、1972 年和 1962 年发生过。

paras.en: In recent decades, each Atlantic hurricane season has averaged seven of these storms. Just two documented seasons—1914 and 1907—went by without any. However, experts note that early weather records are unreliable given the lack of monitoring via satellites or aircraft at the time. Weather watchers could have missed hurricanes in more remote parts of the ocean.
paras.zh: 近几十年来，每个大西洋飓风季节平均有七次此类风暴。只有两个有记录的季节——1914 年和 1907 年——却没有任何进展。然而，专家指出，由于当时缺乏卫星或飞机的监测，早期的天气记录并不可靠。天气观察者可能会错过海洋更偏远地区的飓风。

paras.en: So, what does the growing El Niño have to do with all of this?
paras.zh: 那么，日益严重的厄尔尼诺现象与这一切有什么关系呢？

paras.en: “We are headed toward what will almost certainly be the strongest El Niño on record,” explains Brian McNoldy, a hurricane researcher at the University of Miami, to Ava Berger at NPR. “It has exceeded expectations” in both the Pacific and the Atlantic oceans.
paras.zh: 迈阿密大学飓风研​​究员布莱恩·麦克诺迪 (Brian McNoldy) 向美国公共广播电台 (NPR) 的艾娃·伯杰 (Ava Berger) 解释道：“我们几乎肯定会迎来有记录以来最强烈的厄尔尼诺现象。”太平洋和大西洋都“超出了预期”。

paras.en: The natural, cyclical climate pattern warms ocean waters in the Pacific, which in turn impacts the global climate in myriad ways. In the North Atlantic, it typically increases wind shear—changes in wind speed or direction in the atmosphere. These winds rip apart storms, stopping them from growing into hurricanes. Since this summer, the shear has been record-strong over parts of the Atlantic where hurricanes often form, Klotzbach tells CNN.
paras.zh: 自然的周期性气候模式使太平洋海水变暖，进而以多种方式影响全球气候。在北大西洋，它通常会增加风切变——大气中风速或风向的变化。这些风会撕裂风暴，阻止它们发展成飓风。克洛茨巴赫告诉美国有线电视新闻网，自今年夏天以来，飓风经常形成的大西洋部分地区的切变强度创历史新高。

paras.en: At the same time, warmer ocean surface temperatures in the Pacific allow more hurricanes to form there. The elevated water temperature heats the air above it, fueling more of these cyclones, writes meteorologist Matthew Cappucci for the Washington Post. As of October 1, the Pacific has experienced 20 named storms, including three hurricanes classified as Category 5—the most intense kind, with wind speeds of at least 157 miles per hour, per CNN. One of them, Hurricane Polo, had one of the fastest intensifications on record in the eastern Pacific, going from tropical storm to Category 5 hurricane within 24 hours on September 22.
paras.zh: 与此同时，太平洋海洋表面温度升高导致更多飓风在那里形成。气象学家马修·卡普奇在《华盛顿邮报》上写道，水温升高会加热其上方的空气，从而助长更多的气旋。据 CNN 报道，截至 10 月 1 日，太平洋地区已经历了 20 场命名风暴，其中包括 3 场被列为 5 级飓风，这是最强烈的飓风，风速至少为每小时 157 英里。其中之一“波罗”飓风是东太平洋有记录以来强度最快的飓风之一，于 9 月 22 日在 24 小时内从热带风暴升级为 5 级飓风。

paras.en: Quick fact: Tropical cyclones, storms, depressions and hurricanes
paras.zh: 速览：热带气旋、风暴、低气压和飓风

paras.en: A tropical cyclone is a rapidly rotating, low-pressure system that forms over tropical or subtropical ocean waters. A tropical depression is a cyclone with winds of 38 miles per hour or less, a tropical storm is one with winds ranging from 39 to 73 miles per hour, and a hurricane is a cyclone with winds of at least 74 miles per hour.
paras.zh: 热带气旋是在热带或亚热带海水上空形成的快速旋转的低压系统。热带低气压是指风速为每小时 38 英里或以下的气旋，热带风暴是指风速为每小时 39 至 73 英里的气旋，飓风是指风速至少为每小时 74 英里的气旋。

paras.en: Threats could still emerge in the Atlantic Ocean, though, since October is historically a busy month for hurricane landfalls in Florida, writes meteorologist John Morales for NBC6. “I can’t rule out a window of a few days in which these hostile conditions for hurricanes will abate.”
paras.zh: 气象学家约翰·莫拉莱斯 (John Morales) 为 NBC6 撰文称，尽管如此，大西洋仍可能出现威胁，因为历史上 10 月是佛罗里达州飓风登陆的繁忙月份。 “我不能排除几天之内飓风的不利条件将会减弱的可能性。”

paras.en: What’s more, the lack of hurricanes doesn’t mean a lack of tropical storms. These can also be destructive, especially as climate change makes cyclones wetter and more destructive. In September, Tropical Storm Fay came close to becoming the season’s first hurricane, writes Lowry on his Substack, but just missed the wind speed threshold for a hurricane. Its status might still get bumped up during a future review by the National Hurricane Center, per Scientific American.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，没有飓风并不意味着没有热带风暴。这些也可能具有破坏性，特别是当气候变化使气旋变得更加湿润和更具破坏性时。洛瑞在他的 Substack 中写道，9 月，热带风暴费伊差点成为本季首场飓风，但刚刚达不到飓风的风速阈值。据《科学美国人》报道，在国家飓风中心未来的审查中，其地位可能仍会得到提升。

paras.en: With two months left until the end of hurricane season, there’s still time for one of these windy, watery events to emerge. “Don’t tune out. Stay informed,” Morales writes. “But fingers crossed that the rest of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season stays as dead as a doornail.”
paras.zh: 距离飓风季节结束还有两个月，这些大风多水的事件仍有时间出现。 “不要忽视。随时了解情况，”莫拉莱斯写道。 “但祝愿 2026 年大西洋飓风季的剩余时间能够保持平静。”

articles.title: A Diver Volunteered to Clean Up Trash From a Wisconsin Lake. He Discovered a 1,000-Year-Old Dugout Canoe at the Bottom Instead

paras.en: Mark Schachtner was just about to wrap up his dive session in Wisconsin’s Pewaukee Lake when he spotted a long object resting on the lake floor. Intrigued, Schachtner swam closer and began to inspect the mysterious object. Within a few seconds, he realized he was looking at a canoe, possibly an extremely old one.
paras.zh: 马克·沙赫特纳 (Mark Schachtner) 正要结束在威斯康星州皮沃基湖 (Pewaukee Lake) 的潜水课程，这时他发现湖底有一个长长的物体。出于好奇，沙赫特纳游得更近，开始检查这个神秘物体。几秒钟之内，他意识到自己看到的是一艘独木舟，可能是一艘非常古老的独木舟。

paras.en: Now, experts with the Wisconsin Historical Society have determined that the vessel is a roughly 1,000-year-old dugout canoe, likely handcrafted and used by Indigenous communities in the late 10th or early 11th century.
paras.zh: 现在，威斯康星州历史学会的专家确定，这艘船是一艘大约有 1000 年历史的独木舟，很可能是在 10 世纪末或 11 世纪初由土著社区手工制作和使用的。

paras.en: Numerous dugout canoes have been found throughout Wisconsin, including 16 in an ancient canoe “parking lot” in Lake Mendota, near the state capital Madison. But the newly discovered vessel is believed to be the first found in Pewaukee Lake, a 2,437-acre, spring-fed body of water located in Waukesha County, on the western outskirts of Milwaukee.
paras.zh: 在威斯康星州各地发现了许多独木舟，其中 16 艘位于该州首府麦迪逊附近门多塔湖的一个古老独木舟“停车场”。但这艘新发现的船只据信是在皮沃基湖 (Pewaukee Lake) 中发现的第一艘船只，皮沃基湖 (Pewaukee Lake) 是一个占地 2,437 英亩的泉水湖，位于密尔沃基西郊的沃克夏县 (Waukesha County)。

paras.en: Schachtner, a 45-year-old member of the 4 Seasons Scuba Diving Club, was participating in a volunteer trash cleanup dive in Pewaukee Lake on May 6 when he spotted the canoe. Immediately, he realized that he had stumbled upon something special. He made note of the vessel’s location and got in touch with Tamara Thomsen, a maritime archaeologist with the society.
paras.zh: 沙赫特纳 (Schachtner) 是 4 Seasons Scuba Diving Club 的 45 岁会员，5 月 6 日，他在皮沃基湖 (Pewaukee Lake) 参加志愿垃圾清理潜水活动时发现了这艘独木舟。立刻，他意识到自己偶然发现了一些特别的东西。他记下了船只的位置，并与该协会的海洋考古学家塔玛拉·汤姆森取得了联系。

paras.en: “It stuck out to me,” Schachtner tells the Wisconsin State Journal’s Barry Adams, adding that he was aware of the dugout canoes previously found by Thomsen and her colleagues in Lake Mendota. “I always keep my eyes peeled. There’s not much for big logs down there unless it’s a fish crib or something. The whole thing was sticking out.”
paras.zh: “这让我印象深刻，”沙赫特纳告诉威斯康星州日报的巴里·亚当斯，并补充说他知道汤姆森和她的同事之前在门多塔湖发现的独木舟。 “我总是睁大眼睛。那里没有太多大木头，除非是鱼床什么的。整个东西都很突出。”

paras.en: Five days after Schachtner’s initial discovery, he and Thomsen returned to the site together to take measurements, snap photos and videos, and collect a small sample of the wood. The vessel, which archaeologists say is in good condition, measures 17.3 feet long by 1.8 feet wide at its thickest point, with 2.5-inch-thick walls and a 4.8-inch-thick bottom.
paras.zh: 沙赫特纳最初发现五天后，他和汤姆森一起回到现场进行测量、拍摄照片和视频，并收集了一小部分木材样本。考古学家称，这艘船状况良好，最厚处长 17.3 英尺，宽 1.8 英尺，壁厚 2.5 英寸，底部厚 4.8 英寸。

paras.en: In August, the society received the results of radiocarbon dating and wood identification tests, which revealed that the canoe was crafted roughly a millennia ago from white oak. Testing revealed a 70 percent chance the canoe was created between 992 and 1049 C.E., an era known to archaeologists as the Late Woodland Period, when the Mississippian culture was flourishing and Indigenous groups were building effigy mounds and growing maize.
paras.zh: 八月，该协会收到了放射性碳测年和木材鉴定测试的结果，结果显示这艘独木舟是大约千年前用白橡木制成的。测试显示，独木舟有 70% 的可能性是在公元 992 年至 1049 年之间制造的，考古学家将这一时期称为林地晚期，当时密西西比文化蓬勃发展，土著群体正在建造雕像土堆并种植玉米。

paras.en: Around this same time, the Cahokia people were expanding into Wisconsin, where they established trading posts and fortified settlements like Aztalan, now Aztalan State Park.
paras.zh: 大约在同一时间，卡霍基亚人向威斯康星州扩张，在那里建立了贸易站和坚固的定居点，如阿兹塔兰（现在的阿兹塔兰州立公园）。

paras.en: To better understand the canoe, the society’s experts are consulting with Larry Plucinski, tribal historic preservation officer for the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa, and Bill Quackenbush, a retired tribal historic preservation officer for the Ho-Chunk Nation. Both are longtime tribal partners on the Wisconsin Dugout Canoe Survey Project, which is being spearheaded by Thomsen and Sissel Schroeder, an anthropologist at the University of Wisconsin, Madison.
paras.zh: 为了更好地了解独木舟，该协会的专家正在咨询苏必利尔奇珀瓦湖巴德河段的部落历史保护官员拉里·普鲁辛斯基（Larry Plucinski）和霍-琼克民族（Ho-Chunk Nation）退休部落历史保护官员比尔·奎肯布什（Bill Quackenbush）。两人都是威斯康星独木舟调查项目的长期部落合作伙伴，该项目由汤姆森和威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的人类学家西塞尔·施罗德牵头。

paras.en: Today, the canoe rests on the lake bottom, roughly 15 feet below the surface. But 1,000 years ago, experts suspect that the site was above water, located along the lake’s ancient shoreline. The vessel was probably parked there intentionally for later use, Plucinski tells the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel’s Caitlin Looby.
paras.zh: 如今，独木舟停泊在湖底，距水面约 15 英尺。但 1000 年前，专家怀疑该遗址位于水面之上，位于湖泊古老的海岸线上。普鲁辛斯基告诉《密尔沃基哨兵报》的凯特琳·卢比，这艘船可能是故意停在那里供以后使用。

paras.en: Dugout canoes were once an essential means of transportation. They were typically shared by the broader community rather than owned by individuals. “It was just common knowledge that nobody owned it,” Plucinski tells the Wisconsin State Journal. “If you needed it, you used it.”
paras.zh: 独木舟曾经是重要的交通工具。它们通常由更广泛的社区共享，而不是由个人拥有。 “众所周知，没有人拥有它，”普鲁辛斯基告诉威斯康星州日报。 “如果你需要它，你就使用它。”

paras.en: The canoe appears to have been carved by hand—possibly using shells or stone tools—and shaped using fire, a process that likely “took a lot of time,” Jon Greendeer, president of the Ho-Chunk Nation, tells Wisconsin Public Radio’s Danielle Kaeding. “You can imagine how much work went into each one of these.”
paras.zh: 独木舟似乎是手工雕刻的——可能使用贝壳或石器——并用火塑造形状，这个过程可能“花了很多时间”，Ho-Chunk Nation 的主席乔恩·格林迪尔 (Jon Greendeer) 告诉威斯康星州公共广播电台的丹尼尔·凯丁 (Danielle Kaeding)。 “你可以想象每一项都需要投入多少工作。”

paras.en: Over the centuries, the canoe was likely exposed to temperature fluctuations, dragging anchors and other disturbances. But it’s partially filled with sediment, which may have helped protect it from damage. “It’s very remarkable that it’s intact and as beautiful as it is,” Thomsen tells the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.
paras.zh: 几个世纪以来，独木舟很可能受到温度波动、拖锚和其他干扰的影响。但它的一部分充满了沉积物，这可能有助于保护它免受损坏。汤姆森告诉《密尔沃基哨兵报》：“它完好无损，而且如此美丽，真是太了不起了。”

paras.en: In accordance with the wishes of Wisconsin’s Indigenous nations, the canoe will remain submerged in the lake. Keeping it underwater will also give the vessel the best chance of preservation, the society notes.
paras.zh: 根据威斯康星州原住民的意愿，独木舟将继续淹没在湖中。该协会指出，将其保持在水下也将为该船提供最好的保存机会。

paras.en: The exact location is being kept private, although local and regional conservation wardens know where it is. Divers may visit the site, but state law prohibits removing, defacing, displacing or destroying the vessel.
paras.zh: 尽管当地和地区的保护管理员知道它在哪里，但确切的位置仍然保密。潜水员可以参观该地点，但州法律禁止拆除、污损、移位或毁坏船只。

paras.en: While this may be the first canoe discovered in Pewaukee Lake, Plucinski suspects it won’t be the last. Given how important the vessels were for transportation, he believes that similar vessels are likely still waiting to be discovered.
paras.zh: 虽然这可能是在皮沃基湖发现的第一艘独木舟，但普鲁辛斯基怀疑这不会是最后一艘。考虑到这些船只对于运输的重要性，他认为类似的船只可能仍在等待被发现。

paras.en: “This might be one of many more people will find,” Plucinski tells the Wisconsin State Journal. “No matter what lake you go to, there’s probably canoes out there.”
paras.zh: “这可能是更多人会发现的其中之一，”普鲁辛斯基告诉威斯康星州日报。 “无论你去哪个湖，那里都可能有独木舟。”

articles.title: New Research Shows That These Ancient Egyptian Servants May Have Been Brutally Sacrificed and Buried Alongside Their Pharaohs

paras.en: Five thousand years ago, some of ancient Egypt’s first royals were laid to rest in grand tombs, accompanied by hundreds of their courtiers. Archaeologists have long puzzled over this arrangement. But a new forensic study published in the journal Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology suggests that these servants may have been prematurely dispatched to the afterlife, where they could serve their rulers for all eternity.
paras.zh: 五千年前，一些古埃及第一批王室成员被安葬在宏伟的坟墓中，身边有数百名朝臣陪伴。考古学家长期以来对这种安排感到困惑。但发表在《环境考古学前沿》杂志上的一项新法医研究表明，这些仆人可能被过早地送往来世，在那里他们可以永远为统治者服务。

paras.en: Study author Roselyn Campbell, a bioarchaeologist at Purdue University, analyzed 46 skulls from Umm el-Qaab, a royal cemetery in Abydos, where Egypt’s first pharaohs were interred.
paras.zh: 该研究的作者、普渡大学生物考古学家 Roselyn Campbell 分析了来自阿比多斯乌姆卡布皇家墓地的 46 个头骨，埃及第一位法老就埋葬在那里。

paras.en: The famed Egyptologist Flinders Petrie first excavated these skulls back in the 1920s, when he discovered hundreds of graves surrounding Abydos’ royal tombs. Reasoning that these retainers (court officials and servants) likely didn’t die of natural causes simultaneously, Petrie suspected they had been sacrificed. But he couldn’t find physical evidence of murder to back up his hunch.
paras.zh: 著名埃及古物学家弗林德斯·皮特里 (Flinders Petrie) 于 1920 年代首次挖掘了这些头骨，当时他在阿比多斯皇家陵墓周围发现了数百座坟墓。皮特里认为这些家臣（宫廷官员和仆人）很可能不会同时自然死亡，因此怀疑他们是被牺牲的。但他找不到谋杀的物证来支持他的预感。

paras.en: Campbell has now reassessed some of the preserved skulls using modern forensic methods. She found that 18 of the 46 crania had suffered significant trauma, suggesting that these individuals were “deliberately killed by blows to the head,” per a statement from Frontiers.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔现在使用现代法医方法重新评估了一些保存完好的头骨。根据 Frontiers 的一份声明，她发现 46 名颅骨中有 18 名遭受了严重创伤，这表明这些人是“故意因头部受到打击而死亡”。

paras.en: “This question of whether or not retainer sacrifice was practiced in Egypt has been debated for over a century, but this is the first study to examine the human remains from the tombs themselves,” Campbell tells the Guardian’s Nicola Davis.
paras.zh: “关于埃及是否实行家臣祭祀的问题已经争论了一个多世纪，但这是第一项对坟墓本身进行人类遗骸检查的研究，”坎贝尔告诉《卫报》的尼古拉·戴维斯。

paras.en: The retainers were interred in rows of simple “subsidiary burials” surrounding the funerary enclosures of three royals: King Djer (the third pharaoh of Egypt’s First Dynasty, who ruled around 3000 B.C.E.) and two of his successors, King Djet and Queen Meretneith.
paras.zh: 这些家臣被安葬在围绕着三位皇室成员的墓地的一排排简单的“附属墓葬”中：杰尔国王（埃及第一王朝的第三位法老，统治于公元前 3000 年左右）和他的两位继任者杰特国王和梅雷特奈斯王后。

paras.en: “In many cultures, retainer sacrifice is practiced because of beliefs that the sacrificed individuals will continue to serve the ruler in some kind of afterlife, but retainer sacrifice can also be a visceral display of the ruler’s power,” Campbell says in the statement. “Some retainers might have volunteered to die to achieve eternal life or honor. Others may have been chosen or even forced.”
paras.zh: 坎贝尔在声明中表示：“在许多文化中，进行家臣祭祀是因为人们相信牺牲者在来世将继续为统治者服务，但家臣祭祀也可以是统治者权力的发自内心的展示。” “一些家臣可能自愿死去以获得永生或荣誉。其他人可能是被选择的，甚至是被迫的。”

paras.en: The wounds that Campbell identified include multiple linear fractures across cranial vaults, a “penetrative injury” to the side of a head and a “chopping injury” to an eye, per the study. The individuals without skull injuries may have died naturally. Or maybe they were killed via methods such as asphyxiation, which wouldn’t have left skeletal marks for archaeologists to find.
paras.zh: 根据该研究，坎贝尔发现的伤口包括颅顶多处线性骨折、头部侧面的“穿透伤”和眼睛的“砍伤”。头骨没有受伤的个体可能已经自然死亡。或者也许他们是通过窒息等方法被杀死的，这样就不会留下考古学家可以找到的骨骼痕迹。

paras.en: Nobody knows what kinds of weapons the ancient Egyptians used to cause the skull injuries. “Based on comparative forensic and archaeological studies, the most likely implement would have been flat and relatively light, probably made out of something like wood rather than stone,” Campbell tells Live Science’s Owen Jarus.
paras.zh: 没有人知道古埃及人用什么武器造成头骨受伤。 “根据法医和考古学的比较研究，最有可能的工具是扁平且相对较轻的，可能是由木材而不是石头制成的，”坎贝尔告诉《生活科学》的欧文·贾鲁斯。

paras.en: According to the study, the first king of the First Dynasty, Aha, was buried with a few subsidiaries. Djer, Djet and Meretneith were then buried with hundreds, clearly taking retainer sacrifice to new heights. But by the beginning of Egypt’s Second Dynasty, around 2730 B.C.E., subsidiary graves had all but disappeared.
paras.zh: 根据研究，第一王朝的第一位国王阿哈与一些附属者一起陪葬。随后，杰尔、杰特和梅雷特内斯与数百人一起下葬，显然将家臣牺牲推向了新的高度。但到了埃及第二王朝初期，即公元前 2730 年左右，附属坟墓几乎消失了。

paras.en: “The practice was short-lived, with people being replaced by statuettes,” Salima Ikram, an Egyptologist at the American University in Cairo who wasn’t involved in the study, tells the Guardian. “Possibly some or all retainers felt that this was a boon and that they would enjoy an eternal life in the service of the god-king, though they might also have resented it, been terrified, and tried to escape this fate.”
paras.zh: “这种做法是短暂的，人们被雕像所取代，”开罗美国大学的埃及古物学家萨利玛·伊克拉姆（Salima Ikram）告诉《卫报》，她没有参与这项研究。 “可能一些或全部家臣都觉得这是一种恩惠，他们将在侍奉神王的过程中享受永生，尽管他们也可能对此感到怨恨、恐惧，并试图逃避这种命运。”

articles.title: You Probably Aren’t Going to Get the Plague
articles.author: Emily Mullin

paras.en: A mysterious death of a woman in Russia following a lab accident has stoked fears about plague spreading. But the odds of that actually happening remain very low, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention saying on X Tuesday afternoon that the circumstances of the case remain unconfirmed and that there is “no indication of a broader threat to the United States” at this time.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯一名妇女在实验室事故后神秘死亡，引发了人们对鼠疫蔓延的担忧。但这种情况实际发生的可能性仍然很低，美国疾病控制与预防中心周二下午表示，该病例的具体情况尚未得到证实，目前“没有迹象表明美国面临更广泛的威胁”。

paras.en: “We are working across the US government to assess developments as additional information becomes available,” the agency said. “CDC and our interagency partners are prepared and will continue to monitor the situation closely.”
paras.zh: 该机构表示：“我们正在与美国政府合作，随着更多信息的出现，评估事态发展。” “疾病预防控制中心和我们的跨机构合作伙伴已做好准备，并将继续密切监视局势。”

paras.en: Last week, a young researcher died from severe pneumonia of “unknown” origin after reportedly breaking a test tube at her workplace, the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Siberia. The hospital that treated her before her death was placed under quarantine, and her coworkers at the lab were isolated, according to Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.
paras.zh: 上周，一名年轻的研究人员因在西伯利亚伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的工作场所打破试管而死于“不明”原因的严重肺炎。据自由欧洲电台/自由电台报道，她死前接受治疗的医院已被隔离，她在实验室的同事也被隔离。

paras.en: Christian Lindmeier, a spokesperson for the World Health Organization, told reporters in Geneva on Tuesday that the group has been in touch with Russian authorities. Based on currently available information, WHO says the public health risk to the general population is very low.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织发言人克里斯蒂安·林德梅尔周二在日内瓦告诉记者，该组织已与俄罗斯当局保持联系。根据目前掌握的信息，世卫组织表示，一般人群面临的公共卫生风险非常低。

paras.en: “I think that’s the correct assessment,” says Gigi Gronvall, an immunologist and senior scholar at the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security. “We don’t know anything about anything right now.”
paras.zh: “我认为这是正确的评估，”约翰·霍普金斯健康安全中心的免疫学家兼高级学者吉吉·格伦瓦尔说。 “我们现在什么都不知道。”

paras.en: Russian authorities have said contact tracing hasn’t yielded any signs of dangerous pathogens spreading, according to the Associated Press. Infamous for causing millions of deaths in Europe during the Middle Ages, plague is rare today. It is caused by the bacteria Yersinia pestis, which is found in wild rodents and their fleas in many parts of the world. It’s spread to humans through the bite of an infected flea and occasionally through direct contact with an infected animal. Antibiotics can cure plague, but they must be started as soon as an infection is suspected.
paras.zh: 据美联社报道，俄罗斯当局表示，接触者追踪尚未发现任何危险病原体传播的迹象。鼠疫在中世纪曾在欧洲造成数百万人死亡，因而臭名昭著，但如今却很少见了。它是由鼠疫耶尔森氏菌引起的，这种细菌存在于世界许多地方的野生啮齿动物及其跳蚤中。它通过受感染跳蚤的叮咬传播给人类，偶尔也通过直接接触受感染的动物传播。抗生素可以治愈鼠疫，但一旦怀疑感染就必须立即开始使用。

paras.en: Pneumonic plague occurs when a person inhales infectious droplets that contain the bacteria. In July 2025, an Arizona man died from pneumonic plague after exposure to infected cats. It can also spread from person to person through respiratory droplets during close contact. But human-to-human transmission is rare, with the last reported occurrence happening in 1924 in Los Angeles. The possibility, though, is why the CDC says it’s important to rapidly identify cases and treat them.
paras.zh: 当一个人吸入含有细菌的传染性飞沫时，就会发生肺鼠疫。 2025 年 7 月，亚利桑那州一名男子在接触受感染的猫后死于肺鼠疫。它还可以在密切接触期间通过呼吸道飞沫在人与人之间传播。但人与人之间的传播很少见，最近一次报道发生在 1924 年的洛杉矶。不过，这种可能性正是疾病预防控制中心表示快速识别病例并治疗它们很重要的原因。

paras.en: “Once you know that somebody has been exposed to it, and even if you have a doubt that somebody has been exposed to it, you can immediately start antibiotics to prevent the person getting afflicted with the disease and to avoid the continuous spread of the disease,” says Rutul Dalal, an infectious disease physician at Penn State Health St. Joseph Medical Center.
paras.zh: “一旦你知道有人接触过这种病毒，即使你怀疑有人接触过这种病毒，你也可以立即开始使用抗生素，以防止该人感染这种疾病，并避免这种疾病的持续传播，”宾夕法尼亚州立大学圣约瑟夫医疗中心的传染病医生鲁图尔·达拉尔（Rutul Dalal）说。

paras.en: Dalal says if the Russian lab worker did die from plague, he is confident that the disease could easily be contained. “With Covid, that was a virus we had not dealt with in the past,” he says. That required novel interventions, while “here, we do have antibiotics to deal with this.”
paras.zh: 达拉尔说，如果俄罗斯实验室工作人员确实死于鼠疫，他相信这种疾病很容易得到控制。 “新冠病毒是我们过去从未处理过的病毒，”他说。这需要新的干预措施，而“在这里，我们确实有抗生素来应对这个问题。”

paras.en: The incident also occurred in a remote part of Russia, which could naturally limit its spread. “Siberia is not exactly Paris,” Gronvall says. “There’s not a lot of travel going back and forth.”
paras.zh: 该事件还发生在俄罗斯偏远地区，自然可以限制其传播。 “西伯利亚并不完全是巴黎，”格伦瓦尔说。 “来回的旅行并不多。”

paras.en: Whether plague is the culprit or not remains an open question. Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s federal public health and consumer protection agency, said “extensive” testing found “no microorganisms associated with the patient’s professional activities.” But the US has urged the country to share as much information as possible, while other nations that share borders or are near Russia, including Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan, have set up quarantine protocols.
paras.zh: 瘟疫是否是罪魁祸首仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。俄罗斯联邦公共卫生和消费者保护机构 Rospotrebnadzor 表示，“广泛”测试发现“没有与患者职业活动相关的微生物”。但美国敦促该国分享尽可能多的信息，而哈萨克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦、乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦等与俄罗斯接壤或邻近的其他国家也制定了检疫协议。
